### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier-window traces; in the later window it runs in about 47 in 100 traces (94 of 200), with about 0.96 occurrences per trace overall — roughly two occurrences per trace that contains it — and it sits around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.39) [OCC001, POS001].
- In the later window, about 76 in 100 of A01's outgoing transitions lead to A04, with smaller shares to A13 (about 10 in 100) and A11 (about 7 in 100); no outgoing transitions from A01 were observed in the earlier window [DIR001].
- The activities that previously fed A04 now often route via A01: A11's outgoing transitions went to A04 in about 96 in 100 cases before versus about 22 in 100 after, with about 76 in 100 now going to A01; A03 to A04 fell from about 53 to about 10 in 100, with about 42 in 100 now going to A01; A10 to A04 fell from about 47 to about 13 in 100, with about 25 in 100 now going to A01. A04 itself, which previously led almost only to A13 (about 99 in 100), now also leads to A01 in about 10 in 100 of its outgoing transitions [DIR005, DIR002, DIR004, DIR003].
- A01 and A04 changed from never co-occurring to always co-occurring: in the later window both appear in about 47 in 100 traces and neither ever appears without the other, with A01 before A04 in about 20 in 100 traces and the two interleaved or repeated in about 23 in 100. A01 also now co-occurs with A03 (about 27 in 100 traces, A03 first in about 15), with A10 (about 20) and with A11 (about 23, almost always interleaved or repeated) [REL002, REL001, REL003, REL004].
- Step distances shifted by roughly one position: A03 to A04 and A10 to A04 moved from mostly one step apart (about 55 and 47 in 100) to mostly two steps (about 62 and 51); A04 to A11, A10 to A11, A03 to A11, and the repetitions of A04 and of A11 moved from mostly three steps apart to mostly four [LAG001, LAG005, LAG007, LAG004, LAG006, LAG002, LAG003, LAG008].
- A04 itself now appears slightly later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.39 before versus about 0.44 after) and in somewhat fewer traces (about 54 in 100 before versus 47 in 100 after) [POS002].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the process executes A01 — not observed in the earlier window — on the paths leading into A04: A11, A03 and A10, which previously led directly to A04 in the large majority of their outgoing transitions, now frequently lead to A01 first, and A01 in turn leads to A04 in about three quarters of its outgoing transitions. As a result, A04 and the activities around it sit about one step later in the trace [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, DIR002, DIR004, DIR003, LAG001, LAG005].

The reading is direct and consistent across participation, position, successor profiles, pairwise relations and step distances, and its overall volume far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 20 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.23 expected by chance, and every item's difference exceeded that of about 199 in 200 random re-splits of the pooled traces [OCC001, DIR005, REL002, LAG001].

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A01 was not executed in those 200 sampled traces, so a previously vanishingly rare presence cannot be excluded; the placement is predominantly but not exclusively before A04 (A01 follows A04 in about 5 in 100 of their joint traces, and the pair is interleaved or repeated in about 23 in 100); and the many items partly restate one underlying restructuring rather than independent confirmations. The competing explanation — sampling fluctuation in an unchanged process — is made unlikely by the number of qualifying items but cannot be excluded for any single item [REL002, OCC001].

Other differences: beyond the rerouting to A01, A10's outgoing transitions also shifted toward A02 (about 15 to 25 in 100) and A07 (about 20 to 28 in 100), and A04 appears in somewhat fewer traces (about 54 versus 47 in 100) [DIR004, POS002].
